material_systems.name: DTM Primer for Steel Garage Doors

primer.type: Acrylic DTM (Direct-to-Metal) Primer with Rust-Inhibitive Pigments
products: Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial DTM Acrylic Primer
PPG Pitt-Tech Plus DTM Industrial Primer
primer.notes: Rust-inhibitive DTM primer with ~46% volume solids. Flash-rust resistant — prevents oxidation while waterborne primer is wet. Flexible for thermal expansion of steel panels. MANDATORY for ALL steel garage doors after wax removal and deglossing — factory primer alone is NOT adequate due to wax contamination. Unlike entry doors where factory-primed steel may skip field prime, garage door factory finish requires DTM overcoat.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for all steel garage doors in NC. Factory-primed steel STILL gets DTM primer because wax removal protocol compromises factory primer reliability. SS_EXT_BARE_METAL is rare in NC (factory primer damaged during transit). Coverage rate is for smooth factory steel surface.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Exterior Primer for Wood Garage Doors

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for bare wood garage doors. Remains flexible, breathable, good adhesion. For non-tannin wood species (pine, fir, spruce). For tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood), supplement with alkyd stain-blocker (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_ALKYD_STAINBLOCK) at knots. Six-side sealing obligation per DASMA TDS #162 — primer must cover all six sides including back face and edges.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for bare wood garage doors. Higher coverage than DTM (smoother absorption on sanded wood). End-grain (top/bottom edges) absorbs more primer — may require heavier application at edges for six-side seal per DASMA TDS #162.

material_systems.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer for Tannin-Rich Wood Garage Doors

products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: Required for cedar, redwood, and Douglas fir garage door panels. Superior tannin stain blocking — alkyd penetrates deep into wood and prevents extractive bleed-through. May be applied as full-surface primer for severe tannin species, or spot-applied at visible knots under full acrylic primer coat. Shellac-based (BIN) for extreme tannin cases. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 2: spot prime knots with alkyd before acrylic over remaining surface.

material_systems.notes: Conditional on wood species. NOT for galvanized metal. Can be spot-applied (knots only) or full-surface depending on tannin severity. When spot-applied, quantity is not SF-based — it is per-knot consumption. Full-surface application on severe species uses stated coverage rate.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Carriage-Style Composite Overlays

primer.type: Bonding Primer for Glossy/Sealed Composite Surfaces
primer.notes: Conditional — only needed when carriage-style overlays have glossy, sealed, or factory-finished composite surfaces that reject standard primers. Grips slick composite while providing mechanical tooth for topcoat. Must be topcoated within 1 week — bonding primer loses flexibility and becomes brittle if left exposed too long. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 3.

material_systems.notes: Applied to composite overlay panels on carriage-style doors. Steel base of carriage doors gets DTM primer (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_DTM). This bonding primer is for the overlay material only. Conditional on overlay surface condition.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Latex for Garage Doors

products: Benjamin Moore Regal Select Exterior Paint
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Acrylic Latex
finish.notes: Mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior latex. Superior UV resistance, flexibility for thermal expansion, excellent adhesion over properly primed surfaces. Works on all three substrates (steel, wood, carriage) — same topcoat chemistry regardless of substrate. 2 coats standard. Leapfrog technique mandatory for sectional articulation. Sheen is project-level selection (satin, semi-gloss, gloss) per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md.

material_systems.notes: QT3 standard finish for all garage door substrates. Coverage rate accounts for spray application on factory-smooth or primed surfaces. Same material on steel, wood, and carriage — substrate-specific behavior is handled by the primer system, not the topcoat.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic Latex for Garage Doors

products: PPG Manor Hall Exterior Premium Acrylic
finish.notes: Premium 100% acrylic with enhanced UV resistance, self-cleaning technology, superior color retention and fade resistance. Higher solids content for better film build. 2 coats with light 220-grit sand between finish coats (QT4 requirement). Leapfrog technique mandatory. Raking light inspection for runs/sags/holidays between coats. Sheen is project-level selection.

material_systems.notes: QT4 premium finish for upscale garage doors — carriage-style, wood panel, and steel on custom homes. Same application technique as standard but with interstage sanding and premium inspection. Higher durability justifies premium material cost on large exposed surfaces.

ea_conversion.notes: Single door: 8x7 or 9x7 ft = 56-63 SF exterior face. Double door: 16x7 or 18x7 ft = 112-126 SF exterior face. Garage door EA covers exterior face only — back face is separate scope if applicable.

single.notes: 60 SF single door face at 375 SF/gal = 0.16 gal. Smooth factory steel surface — non-porous, consistent coverage.

double.notes: 119 SF double door face at 375 SF/gal = 0.32 gal.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% waste factor for garage door spray application. Higher than entry doors (10%) because larger surface with more overspray at panel edges and articulation joints during leapfrog technique.

spray_transfer_efficiency.notes: Spray at 60-70% transfer efficiency on garage door faces. Slightly lower efficiency than entry doors due to panel recesses and articulation gaps catching overspray. Budget 33-40% more material than theoretical brush coverage.

ea_conversion.notes: Same SF as steel doors. Wood doors may have slightly more surface area due to raised panel profiles. Six-side sealing adds back face + edge SF but that is handled as separate material allocation.

single.notes: 60 SF single door at 425 SF/gal = 0.14 gal (exterior face only). End-grain edges absorb more — add 5-10% for edge application.

double.notes: 119 SF double door at 425 SF/gal = 0.28 gal (exterior face only).

six_side_seal_adder.notes: DASMA TDS #162 six-side sealing adds back face + top/bottom/side edges. Back face is ~equal to front face SF. Edges add ~10-15 SF. Primer on back face and edges is sealing obligation — 1 coat. Total additional material is roughly 50-60% of front face primer.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% waste factor. Wood absorbs more at end-grain (top/bottom edges) — six-side sealing increases effective consumption.

spray_transfer_efficiency.notes: Same transfer efficiency as steel. Wood grain texture does not significantly affect spray efficiency on primed surfaces.

ea_conversion.notes: Finish coat on primed surface — sealed, non-porous, consistent coverage regardless of substrate. All substrates produce similar coverage on primed surface.

SYS_EXT_GRDR_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard acrylic on primed door. 2 coats. Total per single door: ~0.34 gal. Total per double door: ~0.68 gal.

SYS_EXT_GRDR_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium acrylic — same coverage rate as standard. Higher solids give better film build per coat but similar spread rate. 2 coats with interstage sand.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% waste factor for finish coats. Spray overspray at panel edges and articulation joints.

spray_transfer_efficiency.notes: Same transfer efficiency as primer. Leapfrog technique with panel articulation creates additional overspray loss at joint gaps.

consumables.name: 3M Gray Synthetic Steel Wool Pad (#000 equivalent)
consumables.usage_rate: 2 EA per single door, 3 EA per double door
consumables.notes: For factory wax removal on steel garage doors. Saturated with biodegradable cleaner per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2. Gray synthetic (NOT real steel wool — ferrous residue causes rust staining). Pads wear quickly on textured factory finishes. Spec-unique consumable — no other spec requires synthetic steel wool. Steel substrate only.

consumables.name: Biodegradable Degreaser / TSP-Substitute Cleaner
consumables.notes: Cleaning solution for wax removal protocol on steel doors (with CON_GRDR_STEEL_WOOL_PAD). Also serves as general surface cleaner for all substrates. TSP-substitute preferred for environmental compliance. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-150 Grit (medium sanding block)
consumables.notes: For deglossing factory finish on steel doors (120-150 grit per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2). Also for sanding bare wood doors to clean profile. Medium sanding block. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit (fine sanding block)
consumables.notes: Intercoat sanding between finish coats — QT4 only. Light scuff sand with raking light inspection. QT3 does visual inspect only, no intercoat sand. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Required after all sanding operations (degloss, intercoat). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 310 (garage door faces)
consumables.notes: 310 tip (0.010 inch orifice, 6-inch fan) for metal garage door faces. Tight fan for precision on discrete panel surfaces. Also suitable for 412 tip (0.012 inch, 8-inch fan) on larger double-door faces. Per Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine: metal doors use 0.010-0.014 inch orifice. 100-mesh blue filter for enamel on steel. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: 100-Mesh Spray Filter (blue) for Enamel on Steel
consumables.notes: Fine 100-mesh (blue) filter for spraying enamel/acrylic on steel garage doors. Finer than standard 60-mesh latex filter — prevents nozzle clog from pigment particles in DTM and enamel formulations. Change when flow rate drops. Only applicable when application_method = spray and substrate = steel.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2.5 inch
consumables.notes: For brush detail work on raised panel recesses, carriage overlay edges, window frame edges, and six-side seal edge work on wood doors. 2.5-inch angular sash per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md. 1 brush per material type. ~5,000 LF lifespan with care. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade, UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for exterior exposure. Used for: weatherstrip gap taping, track/hardware edge masking, window insert edge seal, siding masking edges, bottom seal zone taping. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: all tape rolls yield 180 LF (60 yards). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking Film / Plastic Sheeting (4 mil)
consumables.notes: For adjacent siding masking during spray application. Pre-taped poly or masking film applied to siding panels flanking garage door opening. 4 mil minimum. Also for track/spring mechanism coverage inside garage. NOT for driveway protection (safety hazard — use canvas). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: HDPE Static-Cling Window Masking Film
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA kit per door with window inserts
consumables.notes: HDPE static-cling film for garage door window inserts. Adheres without adhesive — no residue on glass. Covers glass panes to protect from spray overspray. Divided-lite carriage windows require individual pane masking (more film, more time). Conditional — only when windows present. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Canvas Driveway Runner / Absorbent Mat
consumables.notes: Driveway/apron protection for spray operations. Canvas drop cloths or absorbent mats provide non-slip surface on hardscapes. Standard poly sheeting is a SAFETY HAZARD on driveways — becomes slippery when wet with paint. Canvas absorbs drips while maintaining foot traction. Single door: 1 runner. Double door: 2 runners or 1 oversized. Per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 7 and Exterior_Protection_Doctrine_T3.md section 2.

consumables.name: Canvas Drop Cloths (supplemental)
consumables.notes: Supplemental canvas drops for extended driveway protection beyond runners, and for catch areas during bottom-edge painting. Non-slip, absorbent surface. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Low-Tack Weatherstrip Protection Tape
consumables.notes: Low-tack tape for masking weatherstripping contact surfaces along sides and top of garage door. Pushed into weatherstrip channel with putty knife. Prevents paint contamination of weatherstrip — paint destroys seal flexibility. ~35-40 LF of weatherstrip per garage door. 180 LF per roll. Per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 7.

consumables.name: Exterior Wood Filler
consumables.notes: For filling small defects, nail holes, and minor damage on wood garage door panels. Exterior-rated filler that remains flexible through thermal cycles. Wood substrate only. Most NC wood doors have minimal defects.

ext_garage_driveway_apron.description: Driveway/apron surface below garage door requiring protection during spray operations
ext_garage_driveway_apron.notes: Full cover mandatory for spray operations. Canvas drops or absorbent mats ONLY — standard poly is a safety hazard on hardscapes (slippery). Broom-finish concrete is porous and absorbs paint permanently. Decorative pavers have joints that trap paint. Protection scope extends 6-8 feet from door base.

ext_garage_siding_adjacent.description: Siding panels adjacent to garage door opening requiring masking during spray
ext_garage_siding_adjacent.notes: Pre-taped poly or masking film on siding flanking the garage door opening. No separate PS key for siding SF — masking is included in per-door setup estimate. Material quantity scales with door count, not siding area.

ext_garage_window_mask.description: Window inserts in garage door panels requiring masking
ext_garage_window_mask.notes: HDPE static-cling film on window panes. Edge seal with blue tape at glass-to-frame junction. Carriage-style divided-lite windows require individual pane masking — significantly more material and time than standard top-panel window inserts.

ext_garage_weatherstrip.description: Weatherstripping along sides and top of garage door requiring masking
ext_garage_weatherstrip.notes: Low-tack tape into weatherstrip channel with putty knife. Paint on weatherstripping destroys seal flexibility — causes brittleness and seal failure. ~35-40 LF of weatherstrip per door (sides + top). Per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 7.

ext_garage_track_hardware.description: Track, roller, and spring mechanism hardware requiring masking
ext_garage_track_hardware.notes: Track and roller contact points, spring mechanism, cables, brackets — must NOT be painted (causes binding and mechanical failure). Tape + plastic to cover hardware areas visible from spray zone. Masking quantity is per door, not per component.

ext_garage_bottom_seal.description: Bottom weatherseal (astragal) requiring protection or removal during painting
ext_garage_bottom_seal.notes: Bottom seal either removed before painting (preferred) or masked in place. If left in place, tape protects seal from paint contact. Door must be propped 2-4 inches above threshold during 24-48 hour cure to prevent seal bonding to wet paint on driveway surface. Per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 7.

compatibility_rules.description: DTM primer mandatory for all steel garage doors — factory primer is NOT adequate alone
compatibility_rules.notes: Unlike entry doors where factory-primed steel may skip field prime, garage door factory finish has wax contamination making factory primer unreliable. DTM primer mandatory after wax removal + degloss. Acrylic latex primer on steel causes flash rust. Per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 4.

compatibility_rules.description: Acrylic primer for wood — alkyd stain-blocker required for tannin-rich species
compatibility_rules.notes: All bare wood gets acrylic primer. Tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir) additionally require alkyd stain-blocker spot-prime at knots BEFORE full acrylic coat. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 2.

compatibility_rules.description: Tannin spot-prime for cedar, redwood, and fir species
compatibility_rules.notes: Spot-applied at visible knots before full acrylic primer. For severe tannin species, may be applied full-surface instead. Prevents brown/yellow stain bleed-through on finish coat.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer conditional for carriage composite overlays
compatibility_rules.notes: Only needed when carriage overlays have glossy/sealed composite surfaces. Standard composite overlays with porous/matte surface can use DTM primer directly. Steel base of carriage door gets DTM primer regardless.

compatibility_rules.description: LRV > 55 HARD STOP for carriage and composite garage doors
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD STOP: Dark colors (LRV < 55) absorb excessive solar energy on carriage/composite doors — causes warping, shrinkage, overlay delamination, voided warranties. Per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 4. If homeowner insists on dark color, require written warranty waiver and IR-reflective coating.

compatibility_rules.description: LRV > 30 recommended for steel garage doors — IR-reflective below 30
compatibility_rules.notes: Steel doors are more tolerant of dark colors than carriage/composite due to metal thermal conductivity. LRV > 30 recommended. Below LRV 30, recommend IR-reflective coating to reduce surface temperature and extend coating life. Not a hard stop for steel — advisory warning.

compatibility_rules.description: Six-side sealing mandatory for wood garage doors per DASMA TDS #162
compatibility_rules.notes: All six sides of wood garage door panels must be primed and sealed. Unsealed end-grain (top/bottom edges) causes moisture wicking, rot, panel distortion, and warranty voidance. Back face gets primer + 1 coat minimum. Per DASMA TDS #162 and Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 4.

compatibility_rules.description: No roller on metal garage doors — introduces orange peel
compatibility_rules.notes: Roller application on smooth factory-finish steel doors introduces orange peel texture. Spray is PRIMARY method for all garage door substrates. Roller AVOIDED on metal per Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine. Brush only for panel recess detail work.

compatibility_rules.description: Bare steel must be primed same day as surface prep
compatibility_rules.notes: Bare ferrous metal begins rusting within hours in humid conditions. Delay between prep and prime voids surface preparation and requires re-prep. Schedule prep and prime as continuous task — do not break across days.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer must be topcoated within 1 week
compatibility_rules.notes: Bonding primer left exposed too long dries brittle — loses flexibility needed for topcoat adhesion. Must apply topcoat within 1 week of primer application. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 5.

risk_notes.topic: Catastrophic peeling from residual factory wax on steel doors
risk_notes.risk: New acrylic paint applied over residual factory wax or Kynar finish without proper wax removal and DTM primer. Entire paint film peels in sheets within weeks.
risk_notes.mitigation: Mandatory wax removal protocol: gray 3M synthetic steel wool pad + biodegradable cleaner. Followed by degloss (120-150 grit). ASTM D3359 adhesion verification. DTM primer before topcoat.

risk_notes.topic: Articulation joint paint bridging — door glued shut
risk_notes.risk: Painting door in closed position bridges paint across panel articulation joints. Opening tears paint film at every joint. Repeated bridging binds door, damages opener motor.
risk_notes.mitigation: MANDATORY leapfrog technique: paint alternating panels (1,3,5 then 2,4,6), opening each joint to dry tack-free before painting adjacent panel. Never paint in fully closed position.

risk_notes.topic: Thermal deformation from dark colors on carriage/composite doors
risk_notes.risk: Dark colors (LRV < 55) absorb excessive solar energy on carriage-style and composite doors. Causes warping, shrinkage, overlay delamination, voided manufacturer warranties.
risk_notes.mitigation: HARD STOP: LRV must be > 55 for carriage/composite doors. Steel doors: LRV > 30 recommended, IR-reflective below 30. Written warranty waiver if homeowner insists on dark carriage color.

risk_notes.risk: Bottom weatherseal (astragal) bonds to wet paint on compression surface against driveway threshold. Opening tears seal, damages paint, may pull driveway coating.
risk_notes.mitigation: Prop door 2-4 inches above threshold during 24-48 hour cure. Or remove bottom seal/retainer entirely before painting, reinstall after cure. Emergency: wax paper on driveway as release agent.

risk_notes.topic: Tannin bleed on wood garage doors
risk_notes.risk: Cedar and redwood species release tannin extractives that bleed through acrylic primers, causing brown/yellow staining on finish coat. Sun-exposed panels are worst affected.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply alkyd stain-blocking primer (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_ALKYD_STAINBLOCK) on tannin-rich species. Spot-prime visible knots before full acrylic primer coat.

risk_notes.topic: Wood rot from incomplete six-side sealing
risk_notes.risk: Failure to seal all six sides of wood garage door panels per DASMA TDS #162. Moisture wicks through unsealed end-grain and back surfaces causing rot, panel distortion, warranty voidance.
risk_notes.mitigation: Mandatory six-side sealing. All edges including top, bottom, back face must be primed and finished. Back face access may require painting before installation or door disassembly.

risk_notes.topic: Driveway safety hazard from poly sheeting
risk_notes.risk: Standard plastic sheeting (poly) on driveway/hardscape becomes extremely slippery when wet with paint overspray. Creates fall hazard for crew and homeowners.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use canvas drop cloths or absorbent floor mats ONLY for driveway protection. NEVER standard poly sheeting. Canvas provides non-slip surface while absorbing paint drips.

risk_notes.topic: Track and hardware paint contamination causing binding
risk_notes.risk: Paint on track, rollers, springs, or cables causes mechanical binding. Door stalls, opener motor overloads, springs may snap under increased tension.
risk_notes.mitigation: Mask all track and hardware zones before spray application. Verify no paint on moving parts after painting. Include in final inspection checklist.

risk_notes.topic: Spring balance impact from paint weight
risk_notes.risk: Heavy coatings add measurable weight to door assembly. Out-of-balance door with added paint weight can strain opener motor or snap counterbalance springs.
risk_notes.mitigation: Balance test checkpoint after painting (SOP quality gate). Two coats of standard acrylic rarely add enough weight to affect a properly balanced door, but note for awareness.

material_quantity_notes.ea_based_system: This spec uses EA (each) as the primary UOM. Material quantities are calculated per door assembly. Door size (single/double) is the primary material scaling factor within EA. All quantities in coverage_profiles are per door face (exterior side).
material_quantity_notes.waste_factor: 15% material waste for garage door painting. Higher than entry doors (10%) due to larger overspray area at panel articulation joints during leapfrog technique and at panel recesses on raised/carriage styles.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on garage doors: 60-70% transfer efficiency. Lower than entry doors due to panel articulation gaps and recesses catching overspray. Budget 33-40% more material than theoretical brush coverage.
material_quantity_notes.coat_system: Standard coat system: 1 primer + 2 finish coats for all substrates. No skip-prime path for garage doors — factory-primed steel STILL gets DTM primer. Wood doors add six-side seal material.
material_quantity_notes.six_side_seal_wood: Wood doors per DASMA TDS #162: primer + minimum 1 coat on back face and all edges. Adds ~50-60% additional primer material per door. Back face finish is sealing obligation, not full 2-coat decorative finish.
material_quantity_notes.total_material_estimate_single_steel: Single steel door (QT3): ~0.16 gal primer + ~0.34 gal finish (2 coats) = ~0.50 gal total before waste/efficiency adjustment. With 15% waste + 40% spray loss: ~0.85-0.90 gal total material.
material_quantity_notes.total_material_estimate_double_steel: Double steel door (QT3): ~0.32 gal primer + ~0.68 gal finish (2 coats) = ~1.00 gal total before waste/efficiency adjustment. With 15% waste + 40% spray loss: ~1.60-1.70 gal total material.

assumptions.value: Single: 56-63 SF (60 SF nominal). Double: 112-126 SF (119 SF nominal). Exterior face only.
assumptions.source: Standard garage door dimensions: 8x7/9x7 single, 16x7/18x7 double. Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md section 5.
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms these dimensions. SF includes panel face area — raised panels and recesses add marginal additional surface area (~5%) which is absorbed into the coverage range.

assumptions.value: Factory-primed steel garage doors STILL require DTM primer after wax removal and deglossing
assumptions.note: Explicitly stated in doctrine. This is DIFFERENT from entry doors where factory primer may be adequate. Wax contamination on garage doors makes factory primer unreliable.

assumptions.value: 15% waste factor for garage door spray application
assumptions.source: Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md (10-20% wastage allowance); extrapolated from entry door (10%) + articulation joint overhead
assumptions.note: Doctrine provides 10-20% range. Using 15% for garage doors — higher than entry doors (10%) due to leapfrog articulation gaps and panel recesses, but lower than rough siding (20%). Sibling exterior door spec uses 10% for contained entry doors.

assumptions.value: 60-70% transfer efficiency for airless spray on garage doors
assumptions.source: Research finding RF-012; sibling entry door spec uses 75-80%
assumptions.note: Lower transfer efficiency than entry doors because garage door articulation joints and panel recesses catch overspray. Entry doors are flat, contained items. Garage doors have panel gaps that waste material during leapfrog technique.

assumptions.value: Back face receives primer + 1 finish coat (sealing obligation) — not full 2-coat decorative finish
assumptions.source: Research uncertainty; DASMA TDS #162 requires all six sides sealed
assumptions.note: DASMA TDS #162 says seal all six sides but does not specify number of finish coats on back face. Assumption: 1 coat on back face meets sealing requirement. Full 2-coat back face would be a scope add-on.

assumptions.value: No dedicated IR-reflective finish system defined for garage doors — LRV restrictions are enforced as hard stops instead
assumptions.note: Carriage/composite doors have LRV > 55 hard stop (most dark colors prohibited outright). Steel doors have LRV > 30 advisory. Rather than defining a separate IR-reflective system (as the entry door spec does), garage door enforcement is via color restriction. If IR-reflective is needed for steel doors at LRV < 30, it can reference the entry door IR-reflective system or be added as a future enhancement.

uncertainty_flags.description: Transfer efficiency estimate of 60-70% for garage door spray is lower than entry doors (75-80%). The articulation joint loss during leapfrog technique is estimated but not field-verified.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate against field material consumption data on actual garage door projects. May be higher (closer to 70%) on flush panels and lower (closer to 55%) on raised panel / carriage styles.

uncertainty_flags.description: Six-side seal adder (50-60% of front face primer) is estimated from door geometry — back face ~equal to front, edges add 10-15 SF. Actual back face access and application method may vary.
uncertainty_flags.action: Field calibration needed. Back face may be sprayed before installation (most efficient) or brush-applied after installation (less efficient, more material waste).

uncertainty_flags.description: 3M synthetic steel wool pad consumption (2 per single, 3 per double) is estimated. Pads wear at different rates depending on factory finish hardness and wax thickness.
uncertainty_flags.action: Track pad consumption across first 10-20 steel garage door projects to calibrate.

uncertainty_flags.description: Bonding primer for carriage composite overlays is conditional on 'glossy_composite' overlay surface. The trigger condition is subjective — no industry standard defines the glossy vs. matte threshold for composite overlays.
uncertainty_flags.action: Define a practical field test (e.g., water bead test or adhesion cross-hatch) for determining when bonding primer is needed on carriage overlays.
